newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News-Oct 21.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News-Oct 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australia's major banks are yet to give credit card customers the benefit of the 0.5 percentage point cut in official interest rates on July 31, holding credit card interest rates at their highest margin above mortgage rates since the card market was dereulated just over three years ago. Page 1.

Optus Communications has jointed AT&T and UUNet in negotiations to buy the troubled Internet service provider (ISP) Access One, but it is unclear whether Access One's parent, Solution 6, is prepared to sell Access One separately, with the price tag possiby as high as A$30 million. Page 3.

Australia's four major petrol retailers and their industry body, the Australian Institute of Petroleum, say Woolworths Ltd's proposal to a Senate select committee to defer the deregulation of the petrol retailing sector for six months would only be to Woolworths' advantage. Page 19.

Leading investment managers say the decision to appoint two more shareholder representatives to the Coles Myer Ltd board may make the board too big and may prevent the company realising its full potential. The changes announced on Friday will see 14 diretors on the board, with Solomon Lew stripped of his vice-chairmanship. Page 19.

Due to fly to Brisbane today to consult lawyers and Queensland Government representatives, Aboriginal leader Charles Perkins vowed yesterday that the Mitakoodi people would not give up their claim for land in the area surrounding MIM Holdings' A$350 millin Ernest Henry Copper project. Page 19.

Following the completion today of its A$360 million merger with Golden Shamrock Mines Ltd, London-based Ashanti Gold Mines will be the first foreign company to trade under the Australian Stock Exchange's new CUFS settlement provisions, which permit electrnic settlement of trades in foreign listed corporations trading on the ASX. Page 20.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Despite United States advisory firm Institutional Shareholder Services declaring against him, Australian National Industries Ltd director Peter Joseph continues to be confident of winning a showdown with his rival Ross Palmer at today's annual meeting. Page 17.

The release of the September quarter consumer price index on Wednesday and average weekly earnings data for August on Thursday look likely to strengthen the prospect of a pre-Christmas cut in official interests rates, with the data likely to show that infation remains firmly under control. Page 17.

Reading Cinemas Australia chief executive John Rochester said his company, the aspiring third force in the Australian cinema industry, is intent on making its debut in the domestic market next year, despite a Victorian Government planning committee's recet rejection of Reading's application to create a freestanding, 25-screen cinema complex in Melbourne's Burwood. Page 17.

The Queensland Government-owned Port of Brisbane authority will hold talks with the Federal Government this week in an attempt to join the second stage in the sale of the Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth airports, despite being excluded last week from the Goernment's list of preferred bidders. Page 19.

A survey by the Australian Society of Certified Practising Accountants has found small businesses have downgraded their expectations for the next 12 months, after experiencing no improvement in operating conditions in the first six months under the HowardGovernment. Page 19.

-- The Full Federal Court has rejected Westpac Banking Corporation's appeal against an earlier judgement on a fringe benefits tax liability. The decision, which relates to whether waived establishment fees on loans offered to Westpac staff should be taxed, will affect all financial institutions that offer loan benefits to staff. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Market economists are expecting low inflation and wages figures this week, with the consumer price index expected to fall from 3.1 per cent to 2.3 per cent, and the underlying inflation rate to fall from 3.1 per cent to 2.5 per cent. The figures could men a pre-Christmas cut in interest rates for business and home borrowers. Page 33.

Australian National Industries Ltd has been issued with a query from the Australian Stock Exchange over the controversial ABT acquisition, in the lead up to today's annual general meeting which will see the conflict between ANI directors Peter Joseph and Ross Palmer come to a head. Page 33.

The Australian subsidiary of United States technology company VeriFone is about to launch a personal ATM which can be used in the home by inserting it into a telephone plug. Rather than dispensing cash in the home, the "P-ATM" will transfer digital cash alue from an account on to the computer chip of a stored-value or "smart" card. Page 35.

The prospects of troubled French mine Salsigne have been improved by Eltin Ltd, a 51 per cent owner of Salsigne, with the company becoming cash flow positive in the September quarter and recording higher gold production. Page 35.

The Full Federal Court has dismissed an appeal by Westpac Banking Corporation against a trial judge's decision that the bank was liable to pay fringe benefits tax on the waiver of loan establishment fees for staff home loans. With the Tax Office set to collect about A$900,000 in additional FBT from the bank, the decision will cause some concern in the banking industry. Page 35.

Anyone with an interest in the sharemarket will be nervous today, as it is nine years since the stockmarket crash of 1987, when the Australian sharemarket lost A$55 billion. Many are comparing the situation in 1987 to the situation in 1996, especially inthe United States, which on Friday night recorded its 31st record high for the calendar year. Page 36.
THE AGE

Australia could face a drop in coal and iron exports following a warning from Japanese steel makers that they would produce less next year. On the eve of the Australia-Japan Business Cooperation Committee's annual two-day meeting, president John Ralph sad the steel makers wanted to deplete stocks they had built up over the past four years of slow growth. Page C1.

The Australian Stock Exchange has issued Australian National Industries Ltd with a query over the controversial 1991 acquisition of the waste-to-energy business ABT from Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press. The ASX has asked ANI to explain why it did not inclue information on the indemnity it gave Holter - the subsidiary that acquired ABT - in annual reports prior to 1996. Page C1.

After the release of a new US medical study on smoking and lung cancer triggered a sell-off in US tobacco stocks, with the share price of top cigarette maker Philip Morris plummeting by 5.5 per cent, Australia's listed tobacco groups could today face plunging prices. Page C1.

The latest Australian Society of Certified Practising Accountants' small business health index rose from 104.7 in the June quarter to 106 in September, indicating that the overall health of small businesses is improving. However, in response to an additinal question in the survey, nearly 90 per cent of respondents said conditions are no better or have worsened since the Howard Government was elected in March. Page C2.

Gold Mines of Australia Ltd reported improved production and reduced operation costs at all its sites in the September quarter, with production of both gold and copper up by about 15 per cent on the June quarter and gold output of 38,770 ounces and copper conentrate production from the redeveloped Mount Lyell mine in Tasmania of 20,544 tonnes. Page C3.

Bankers Trust Australia has notified the stock exchange that it has lifted its holding in Foodland Associated from 6.4 million shares (6.3 per cent) to just under 14 million shares, identifying it as the buyer of the Foodland shares sold by Alan Newman's nnerhadden last Monday at A$5.55 a share. Page C3.
-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
